plays.name: Inside Zone Right
plays.concept: Zone run. Combination blocks create vertical movement; the back picks the crease.

RB.aim: Inside leg of the play-side guard
RB.read: First down lineman past the center: bang the crease, bend behind the center, or bounce

plays.read: No quarterback read in the base version. Tag it as zone read to leave the back-side end for the quarterback.
coachingPoints: Covered linemen block their man; uncovered linemen help play side, then climb to a linebacker.
The back presses the line before he cuts. A cut made too early lets linebackers fit.
The back-side cutoff is what makes the cutback lane.

plays.name: Outside Zone Right
plays.concept: Wide zone. Stretch every gap sideways until one opens; one cut and go.

RB.aim: Outside leg of the tight end
RB.read: End man on the line, then the next defender inside: bounce if reached, bang if the edge is set, bend if the defense over-runs

plays.read: After the handoff the quarterback carries out the bootleg fake to hold the back-side end.
coachingPoints: Linemen win with their second step. If the defender cannot be reached, run him to the sideline.
The back makes one cut and gets vertical. No dancing.
Every bootleg and play-action pass in this family must start with these same steps.

plays.name: Power Right
plays.concept: Gap run. Down blocks play side, the fullback kicks out the end man, the back-side guard pulls through the hole.

RG.target: play-side defensive tackle to the back-side linebacker

RT.target: play-side defensive tackle to the back-side linebacker

RB.aim: Play-side B gap, inside the kick-out

plays.read: None. The play wins on angles and an extra blocker at the point of attack.
coachingPoints: The double team moves the tackle first; one blocker comes off only when the linebacker shows.
The pulling guard stays square and reads the kick-out: inside it if the end widens, around it if he squeezes.
The back is patient for one step so the puller clears, then downhill.

plays.name: GT Counter Right
plays.concept: Gap run with misdirection. The back-side guard kicks out, the back-side tackle wraps, the quarterback reads the unblocked back-side end.

RB.read: Follow the tackle through the hole

plays.read: The back-side end is unblocked because both pullers left. He stays home: give. He chases the pullers down the line: the quarterback keeps and runs where he left.
coachingPoints: The back's counter step holds the linebackers long enough for the down blocks to seal them.
The guard kicks out the first defender to show past the tight end; if that defender squeezes, log him and the tackle goes around.
Down blocks must stop penetration, which kills pullers.

plays.name: Slant-Flat
plays.concept: Quick-game horizontal stretch on the flat defender, mirrored on both sides.

RB.target: first linebacker to show, inside out

plays.read: Pick a side before the snap by leverage and space. Read the flat defender: he widens with the flat, throw the slant; he sits in the slant window, throw the flat.
coachingPoints: The slant must win inside and stay skinny; drifting upfield brings the safety into the play.
The ball is out on the quarterback's first hitch. Against Cover 2 the squat corner sits on the flat and the hook defender closes the slant.
The slant is the hot throw against pressure.

plays.name: Stick
plays.concept: Quick-game triangle to the three-receiver side: a clearing fade, a flat, and a stick route.

RB.target: first linebacker to show, inside out

plays.read: Fade is an alert against press with no safety over the top. Then read the flat defender: he widens with the flat, throw the stick; he hangs inside on the stick, throw the flat.
coachingPoints: The stick runner turns out against a defender inside him and sits against one outside him.
A completion for 5 yards on first down is a win.
X on the back side is the answer when the defense overplays trips.

plays.name: Smash
plays.concept: High-low on the cornerback: a hitch underneath him, a corner route behind him.
plays.read: Read the cornerback on the chosen side: he sinks under the corner route, throw the hitch; he squats on the hitch, throw the corner into the hole behind him.
coachingPoints: The corner route is thrown to a spot away from the safety, at about 20 yards near the sideline.
Against Cover 3 the deep-third corner is already over the top, so take the hitch.
Against Quarters the safety or a Palms corner takes the corner route away.

plays.name: Four Verticals
plays.concept: Four receivers on vertical landmarks. More deep threats than a one- or two-deep coverage has deep defenders.
plays.read: One deep safety: hold him with your eyes and throw the seam he leaves, on a line at 18 to 22 yards. Two deep safeties: a seam bends across the middle between them, or throw the hole shot outside against Cover 2.
coachingPoints: Landmarks matter: outside receivers on the bottom of the numbers, seams 2 yards outside the hashes.
The seam ball is thrown before the receiver clears the linebackers, not lofted.
It needs time. Check the ball down against pressure.

plays.name: Mesh
plays.concept: Two shallow crossers rub underneath, with a corner route over the top and the back on a wheel.
plays.read: Against man: throw the crosser who comes free off the rub, hitting him on the run. Against zone: the crossers settle in the windows between the hook defenders. The corner route is the alert against a squat corner, the wheel against a linebacker in man.
coachingPoints: The tight end sets the depth of the mesh at 6 yards; the slot passes under him close enough to touch.
Crossers keep running against man and sit down against zone.
It is a five-man protection, so the ball must come out against pressure.

plays.name: Dagger
plays.concept: A seam clears the deep middle, a deep dig comes in behind it, and a drag holds the hook defenders down.
plays.read: The seam is an alert if the safeties split wide. Then read the hook defender on the dig side: he sinks under the dig, throw the drag; he jumps the drag, throw the dig into the space behind the linebackers.
coachingPoints: The seam must threaten the safety to carry him out of the dig window.
The dig is flat across the field at 15 and thrown as the receiver clears the hook defender.
It is a long-developing play: protect it, or call it when the rush is contained.

plays.name: Play-Action Boot Flood
plays.concept: Fake outside zone left, quarterback boots right to three receivers at three depths.
plays.read: Low to high on the boot side: the flat now, then the crosser at 12 to 15 yards, then run. The go route is an alert if the deep-third defender is beaten.
coachingPoints: The first two steps of every lineman and the back are identical to outside zone.
The tight end blocks down for a count before releasing to the flat, so the end loses him.
The back-side end is unblocked. If he does not chase the run fake, the quarterback throws the flat immediately or throws it away.

plays.name: Inside Zone Glance RPO
plays.concept: Inside zone with a skinny post behind the weak-side conflict defender, and a bubble as the pre-snap gift.

RB.aim: Inside leg of the play-side guard
RB.read: First down lineman past the center

plays.read: Before the snap: if nobody covers the slot, throw the bubble. After the snap, ride the mesh and read the weak hook defender: he steps up to fit the run, pull and throw the glance behind him; he stays in the throwing lane, hand off.
coachingPoints: The ball must be out quickly: linemen may be only 1 yard downfield.
The glance breaks on the fifth step at a shallow angle, behind the linebacker and in front of the safety.
Against man coverage there is no conflict defender, so it is a handoff.
